title: Damage Report
text: We’ve given up on defeating the Spirit Tortoise and returned to Melromarc to confirm the Phoenix’s whereabouts.
“Welcome back, Lord Iwatani.”

In the strategy room, the Queen—who was managing the chaos within the castle—welcomed my Father. It seems even more chaotic than last time. Word has likely already reached us that even the Spirit Tortoise has been revived.
“Regarding the latest developments… have you… heard anything?”
The Queen nodded in response to my Father’s question.
“I hear that, following the Phoenix, the Spirit Tortoise’s seal has also been broken.”
“So the news has already reached us. And—”

My Father explained that if we were to challenge and defeat the Spirit Tortoise alongside us, we would also have to defeat the Phoenix. The Queen seemed to immediately grasp just how daunting a task that would be.
“I see. We received intelligence that the Spirit Tortoise was fighting someone and had temporarily halted its advance—so it was you and Lord Iwatani, wasn’t it?”

“Yeah… but just defeating the Spirit Tortoise isn’t enough; it’ll come back to life right away. This is just a guess, but we’ll have to defeat the Phoenix at the same time. Has anything come in regarding the Phoenix’s whereabouts?”

After all, we’d been on the move to defeat the Phoenix. I wonder how many times I’ve asked this now. No matter how many times I ask, perhaps because the information is confusing, we still haven’t pinpointed the Phoenix’s location. In the first world, we defeated it the moment it appeared. If we don’t engage it in battle, we have absolutely no idea what actions it might take.
“We’ve been checking. However…”

The Queen looks pale. I wonder what happened. There’s a model shaped like the Phoenix placed on the map. It must have been made within the last few days. But… why is that? The two phoenixes are placed apart from each other.
“Could it be… that the phoenixes are acting separately?”
“…Yes.”

My father pressed his hand to his forehead and groaned. Even I can figure this out. In this situation, where the phoenixes—which I thought were acting together—are moving separately, and even the Spirit Tortoise is active… The only plausible explanation is that even if we defeat just one Phoenix, it will simply revive.

If we could defeat the stronger of the Four Spirits—the one with the higher number—and it wouldn’t revive, there might still be hope, but that’s just wishful thinking. And if we defeat one Phoenix, the other will explode.
“Reports indicate that over the past four days, the Phoenixes have brought down 10 cities, 8 forts, and 7 castles.”

After all, the flying phoenixes have far greater mobility than the Spirit Tortoises. It’s practically as if they’re flying all over the world. Just chasing them down is a challenge. I suppose I could track them to some extent if I rode on a Rival’s back… but aside from the obvious stamina issue, there’s no way I could ever ride one. I’d go into a panic from hives. If they get within range, I think I could take them down with my Brionac or Gungnir.
“Three nations have already cut off communication, and one nation in the direction of the Spirit Tortoise as well…”
The Queen’s words cause the mood here to drop even further. The situation is becoming desperate. Could this… be leading to an outcome even worse than the first world…?
“Based on what Lord Iwatani said, we’d need at least three units to take down the Phoenix and the Spirit Tortoise at the same time—wasn’t that what Lord Iwatani was about to propose?”
“Yes. Specifically, Motoyasu-kun’s Filolials would handle the Spirit Tortoise, Motoyasu-kun would take out one of the Phoenixes, and the remaining one… wait, no—if we take down the Phoenixes…”

I see. So the Filolial unit led by Yuki-chan and the others will take on the Spirit Tortoise. And at the same time, I’ll take down one of the Phoenixes that’s trying to escape, while my Father endures the explosion from the remaining one before finishing it off. I am a bit worried, though, about whether my Father can actually withstand that explosion. But we can’t let fear get the better of us here.
“If we can just pinpoint the Phoenixes’ locations… I think I can take on the risk if we can’t defeat them on time.”
“The Phoenixes’ explosions cover far too wide an area. If we don’t designate a specific battlefield, the damage will increase.”
“We’ll just have to guide them to a certain extent to buy some time.”

My, this is quite a daunting operation. No matter how strong we are, if our opponents are this troublesome, it’s not just a tough fight—it’s a real struggle. If it were simply a matter of defeating it, I wouldn’t be having this much trouble.
“I understand your plan, Lord Iwatani. But… what should we do about the Allied Forces?”

The Queen seems to be at a loss for how to respond. That’s certainly true. There’s no need to needlessly risk lives in such a dangerous operation. I, too, would prefer not to have Filolial-sama and the others fight if possible.

No matter how high their level, it would be difficult for Filolial-sama alone to withstand the Spirit Tortoise’s Breath. In fact, unless it’s my Father, the Shield Hero, no one could possibly withstand it. Even I deflected it with my spear, but stray shots scattered all over the place. It’s extremely dangerous.
“To be honest, while they aren’t exactly ordinary civilians, people who haven’t received the Hero’s blessing will only be a hindrance.”
“…I agree with what Lord Iwatani says.”
“After that, we’ll capture the moving Phoenix and Spirit Tortoise and defeat them at the agreed-upon time… that’s the ideal scenario.”
“As you command, Lord Iwatani—”
Just as the Queen was about to bow deeply, a messenger entered the room. Why does his expression seem slightly brighter than usual?

“A message. Faubrey views the situation as serious and has ordered the dispatch of the Seven Star Heroes, whom he urgently summoned for tomorrow evening. I’m told the Seven Star Heroes who have already gathered have set out!”
“Tomorrow evening…”
My father is estimating the Phoenix’s location on the map. I’m also making my own judgment based on experience. If we were to chase the Phoenix as is… it moves far too quickly.

It would be extremely difficult to pursue a Phoenix that ignores the terrain. Since we’d have to circle around it from the ground, it’ll take even longer. Plus, predictions are just that—predictions—and if there’s a monster nest or something in the way, we could be way off course.

Furthermore, luring the Phoenix to the right spot to defeat it is crucial. The Phoenix, having split into two, won’t regroup in one place unless we make it explode at least once. That means we’ll have to lure it to a location with minimal collateral damage, which will take even more effort. Ideally, I’d have preferred to defeat it without using the Seven Star Heroes of Faubrey… but realistically, that’s difficult.

Moreover, to minimize damage, it’s hard to keep the Spirit Tortoise held back indefinitely. The portal isn’t exactly right in front of the Spirit Tortoise, so we’ll have to chase after it once it leaps. That’ll take even more effort.
“How many of Faubrey’s Seven Star Warriors are coming?”
“According to our intel, one is coming ahead of the others. They say the rest will be dispatched as soon as contact is established.”
“One… Your Majesty, regarding that Seven Star Warrior—according to Motoyasu-kun—”

My father-in-law told the Queen that in the first world, Takt had monopolized all five of the Seven Star Weapons. He said Takt had that kind of ability and had seized the Seven Star Weapons. Given that situation, the fact that they’re sending a Seven Star Hero here only makes things seem even more suspicious.

“It may sound a bit far-fetched, but judging by what Lord Iwatani and Lord Kitamura have said, it’s probably not a lie. However, given the current situation, we might have to make use of them even if they end up becoming enemies of the world.”
“……You’re right. Honestly, it’s a pretty dangerous gamble, but if the Seven Star Heroes cooperate, I think our chances of success will increase dramatically.”
My father turned to face me, looked me straight in the eye, and spoke in a tone of guidance.
“Motoyasu, this might be hard for you, but you understand this is necessary to improve the situation even a little, don’t you?”
“Yes, sir. We’ll use them to our advantage, and once we’ve defeated the Phoenix and the Spirit Tortoise, we’ll dispose of them, right?”
“No, that’s not it! They aren’t truly evil deep down, are they? If we can talk things out, maybe they’ll… actually fight alongside us as heroes, don’t you think?”

Is that even possible? They’re pretty arrogant—I don’t think they’d be any more willing to listen than Ren or Itsuki. They say you can turn poison into medicine, but I don’t think that guy is a decent person. After all, he’s got ties to the Crimson Swine.
“The Whip Hero is the one with ties to the Crimson Swine.”

“You know quite a lot, don’t you? “Yes. While my daughter, Malty—who’s currently on the run—was studying abroad, she had a physical relationship with Takt Alsaholn Faubrey, who later became the Whip Hero.”
“So… could it be that the princess who ran away is a mole?”
“Impossible. I’ve already eliminated the Crimson Swine. Dead people can’t talk. In other words, there’s no way Takt could know what happened to the Crimson Swine.”
